changes: Basis: supplied v1/v2 descriptions and local SKILL.md, references/method.md, and examples/worked-example.md. This is an offline static assessment; no files changed, migration executed, or database behavior tested.
Concept alignment: Equipment and ASSIGNED_TO are provisionally treated as continuing concepts. No stable concept IDs/IRIs were supplied, so formal identity alignment remains unverified.

Equipment identity: serial → (source_system, asset_id) changes entity identity and uniqueness scope. Preserve serial as a non-unique attribute unless another constraint is explicitly established. Source reuse means serial cannot provide a reliable automatic crosswalk.

custodian_id: nullable → required tightens data validity. Missing values become migration blockers for affected rows; the requirement alone does not establish a foreign key, exactly one active assignment, or agreement with historical assignments.

ASSIGNED_TO: anonymous relationships → assignments identified by assignment_id. Repeated assignments between identical endpoints must remain distinguishable. Endpoint pairs cannot recover missing assignment identities.

Temporal semantics: [valid_from, valid_to) includes the start and excludes the end. Historical, current, and future assignments become distinct query concerns. Existing timeless edges do not establish historical dates.
Version recommendation: treat this as a breaking, major-version transition. Identity changes, mandatory data, and relationship history require explicit migration and consumer acceptance.
compatibility: Semantic — breaking: serial no longer determines Equipment identity, and endpoint equality no longer determines assignment identity. Serial reuse may require splitting formerly conflated equipment; matching composite keys may reveal duplicate source records, but neither operation is justified without evidence. Data — conditional and currently unproven: rows lacking source_system, asset_id, or custodian_id cannot satisfy v2; assignments lacking authoritative assignment_id or temporal evidence cannot automatically become complete historical records. A v1 store may already have rejected, overwritten, or merged reused serials; its snapshot alone cannot recover lost distinctions. Query/API — breaking: serial lookups can return multiple equipment, caches and references must use the composite key, and assignment counts can increase when repeated events are preserved. Current-assignment queries need an explicit time predicate; history queries must retain assignment_id. Legacy scalar serial APIs require an unambiguous lookup or an explicit ambiguity error, never an arbitrary first match. Implementation — unverified: ORM keys, upserts, indexes, imports, exports, CDC, pagination, relationship storage, and client serialization must support composite equipment identity and independently keyed assignments. A backend that identifies relationships only by endpoints cannot preserve the requested history. No concrete consumer inventory, data counts, or native runtime evidence was supplied.
migration: Freeze versioned v1/v2 definitions and retain immutable v1 data, source extracts, relationship records, and ingestion/conflict evidence. Record provenance and reconciliation totals before any future migration.

Resolve model decisions before publication: source_system namespace and normalization; composite-key value types; assignment_id uniqueness scope; relationship direction and endpoints; timestamp precision/timezone; whether null valid_to means open-ended; whether assignment overlaps are allowed; and whether custodian_id denotes the current custodian.

Profile raw source records as well as stored v1 rows. Report reused serials, distinct candidate composite keys per serial, duplicate composite keys, missing required values, unresolved endpoints, and missing assignment IDs/dates. Report counts as unknown until measured.

Build an evidence-backed crosswalk from existing source record references and old identities to composite equipment identities. One serial may map to several equipment. Resolve each relationship using its own source provenance; serial alone cannot choose the correct endpoint.

Obtain missing source_system, asset_id, custodian_id, assignment_id, and dates only from authoritative records or an explicitly approved mapping. Do not invent identifiers, infer asset_id from serial, use a placeholder custodian, or substitute migration time for historical dates.

Keep incomplete or ambiguous records in a traceable unresolved set with reasons and original evidence. Exclusion is not successful migration of those records; full acceptance remains blocked unless a narrower scope is explicitly agreed.

Prepare a separate v2 candidate dataset. Reconnect relationships only through resolved endpoint mappings. Preserve repeated assignments with distinct authoritative IDs; treat identical-ID replays separately from conflicting records. Do not deduplicate by serial or endpoint pair.

Validate composite-key uniqueness/non-nullness, required custodians, endpoint resolution, assignment identity scope, and temporal rules. Propose nonempty intervals with valid_from < valid_to when finite; enforce overlap restrictions only after the business rule is confirmed.

Transition consumers through versioned APIs or an adapter. Use composite keys for references and caches. Allow legacy serial resolution only when unique; reject ambiguous reads and writes. Any dual-write path must receive complete authoritative v2 inputs and have conflict/replay handling.

Gate cutover on complete in-scope reconciliation, zero unresolved identity or endpoint mappings, satisfied required fields and temporal rules, consumer regression results, and a successful rollback rehearsal. Reconcile equipment and assignment mappings rather than expecting equal row counts after legitimate splits. Execution would require separate explicit authorization.
rollback: Retain v1 snapshots, original source records, forward/reverse equipment mappings, assignment mappings, unresolved records, and any transition write log. Before cutover, rollback can discard the candidate v2 dataset while preserving evidence. After cutover, pause writes and reconcile all subsequent changes before restoring or rerouting consumers. A lossless v2-to-v1 conversion is impossible when multiple equipment share serial or repeated assignments require identities/history that v1 cannot represent. Never collapse those records silently. Preserve nonrepresentable changes in a recoverable store and require an agreed reconciliation or temporary read-only strategy. Reversal of merges or splits requires retained source evidence; already-lost v1 history cannot be reconstructed from mappings alone.
regression_cases: All identifiers below are synthetic test fixtures, not values to backfill into real records. Cases are proposed and have not been executed.

Serial collision: serial S-17 appears on (SYS-A, A-1) and (SYS-B, A-2). Expect two Equipment entities, retained serial values, and correctly separated references; legacy S-17 lookup reports ambiguity.
Reuse within one source: (SYS-A, A-1) and (SYS-A, A-2) share S-17. Expect two entities; adding source_system to serial is still insufficient for identity.
Composite-key conflict: two records claim (SYS-A, A-1) with conflicting attributes. Expect a visible conflict requiring evidence-backed reconciliation, not silent overwrite or automatic merge.
Missing identity: a row lacks source_system, asset_id, or both. Expect an unresolved record and blocked v2 admission; no generated IDs or serial substitution.
Missing custodian: identity is complete but custodian_id is null. Expect required-field failure and retained evidence; no placeholder or inference from unrelated assignments.
Ambiguous reconnection: an old edge refers only to reused S-17. Expect unresolved endpoint mapping until source evidence identifies the equipment; do not copy the edge to every candidate.

Missing endpoint: an assignment refers to nonexistent equipment or a missing target under the declared relationship model. Expect failed referential validation, without creating invented endpoint entities.
Repeated assignment: H-4 and H-5 have identical endpoints and distinct valid intervals. Expect both assignments and their histories to survive migration, export/import, and reload.

Assignment replay/conflict: an identical replay of H-4 is idempotent within the agreed ID scope. H-4 reused with conflicting endpoints or dates produces a conflict rather than silently replacing history.

Missing assignment evidence: an old edge has no assignment_id or historical timestamps. Expect unresolved conversion; endpoint pairs, row order, and migration timestamps cannot supply the missing facts.
Half-open boundary: H-4 is [10:00,11:00) and H-5 is [11:00,12:00). At 11:00 only H-5 matches; at 12:00 neither matches. Adjacent intervals do not overlap.

Invalid/open interval: reject reversed intervals and, under the proposed nonempty rule, zero-length intervals. Accept null valid_to as unbounded only if that policy is explicitly approved; do not confuse unknown end time with infinity.
Overlap: H-4 is [10:00,12:00) and H-5 is [11:00,13:00). Detect the overlap; reject it only if the agreed assignment cardinality prohibits concurrency.
Custodian/history consistency: required custodian_id differs from an active assignment target. Apply the confirmed meaning of custodian_id; do not rewrite history merely to make the values agree.

Consumer behavior: composite-key lookup isolates each equipment; serial-only ambiguity is explicit; caches do not cross-contaminate reused serials; current queries exclude expired/future assignments and history queries retain both H-4 and H-5.

Rollback: restore the original v1 snapshot and mappings in a rehearsal. Introduce v2-only equipment sharing serial and repeated assignments afterward; verify they remain recoverable and block any purported lossless reverse conversion.
